entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Third Battle of Kharkov was a series of battles on the eastern front of World War II that took place in Kharkiv, Ukraine, from February 19 to March 15, 1943.

This pivotal conflict marked a crucial moment in the war, with German forces ultimately repelling the Soviet advance and inflicting significant losses on the Red Army.

The battle was characterized by brutal fighting, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The Soviet forces, led by General Nikolai Vatutin, launched a series of attacks against the German-held city of Kharkov, but were unable to break through the enemy lines.

The battle ultimately ended in defeat for the Soviet forces, with the Germans regaining control of the city. The Third Battle of Kharkov was a significant turning point in the war on the eastern front, setting the stage for the continued German advance into Soviet territory.

As General Vatutin himself noted, 'The battle on the Donets was a severe blow to the Soviet army, and it marked the beginning of the end of our advance.'
